newsitem.title: USA: Borg-Warner Automotive sees higher 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Borg-Warner Automotive sees higher 1996 net.

text.p: Borg-Warner Automotive Inc said it expects higher 1996 earnings and expects 1997 profits to benefit from sale of the company's manual transmission operations, which have been a drag on earnings.
Borg-Warner, which supplies engine and transmission systems to vehicle makers, said it is comfortable with analysts' earnings estimates of $3.31 a share to $3.40 for 1996 and $4.20 to $4.40 for 1997.

Asked if he were comfortable with a range of estimates provided by First Call for 1996, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John Fiedler said, "Yes," and asked about a 1997 range, he said "$4.20 to $4.40, I'm very comfortable with."

In October, Borg-Warner agreed to sell its North American transmission business to Transmisiones Y Equipos Mecanicos SA de CV. At that time, Borg-Warner said it would take a fourth quarter charge of $35 million or $1.50 a share as a result of the sale.

Fiedler, speaking to reporters before an analysts meeting here, also said that recent General Motors Corp strikes and related work stoppages had no impact in the 1996 third quarter and he expects no impact in the fourth quarter.
Fiedler also said he does not expect Borg-Warner to benefit or be hurt by the increased outsourcing flexibility in new labor contracts with automakers.
